documents.title: Concept of Operations (ConOps) — General-Purpose Mobile Robot Platform for MARS Research
documents.author: Dhamdhawach Horsuwan
documents.summary: Comprehensive ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 Concept of Operations (15 sections, 14 pages) defining mission objectives (O-01 to O-09), stakeholder classes, operational environments, 5 conceptual configurations (Independent, Cooperative, Composite, Reconfigurable, Mixed), 6 research application domains, 8 workflow phases, 11 operational modes, 7 representative scenarios (Scenarios A–G), safety/maintenance concepts, and 16 open engineering items (OI-01 to OI-16).

versions.author: Dhamdhawach Horsuwan
changes: Initial baseline release of MARS-OPS-001 Concept of Operations (ConOps) aligned with ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 (14-page PDF)
Defined Mission Statement & 9 Operational Objectives (O-01 Research Flexibility through O-09 Operational Reliability)

Established 5 System Configurations (Independent, Cooperative, Composite, Reconfigurable, Mixed) & 6 Research Application Domains (Self-Reconfigurable, Object Transport, Navigation, SAR, Region Sweeping, Cross-Application)
Specified 8 Experiment Workflow Phases, 11 Operational Modes (including Manual Wireless Control & Composite Operation), and 7 Representative Operational Scenarios (Scenarios A–G)
Documented Human-System Interaction, Constraints/Assumptions, Safety & Risk Considerations, Support/Maintenance, 16 Open Issues (OI-01..OI-16), and Engineering Document Relationships

documents.title: Stakeholder Needs and Requirements
documents.author: Dhamdhawach Horsuwan
documents.summary: Identifies the 6 intended stakeholder groups (SH-01 to SH-06), defines a 3-tier stakeholder priority classification (Essential, Important, Desirable), and distinguishes researcher-perspective Research Needs (RN-01 to RN-08) from derived platform Stakeholder Requirements (SR-01 to SR-08).

versions.author: Dhamdhawach Horsuwan
changes: A. Distinguished Research Needs (RN-01..RN-08, expressed from the researcher/stakeholder outcome perspective) from derived Stakeholder Requirements (SR-01..SR-08, expressing expected platform capabilities)

B. Added Section 1: Identified Stakeholders (SH-01 MARS Researchers, SH-02 Robotics & Hardware Developers, SH-03 Software & Algorithm Developers, SH-04 Experimental Operators, SH-05 Laboratory Technicians, SH-06 External Research Collaborators)
C. Added Section 2: Stakeholder Priority Classification (Essential, Important, Desirable) and tagged all 8 Need/Requirement pairs with priorities and primary stakeholders

versions.author: Dhamdhawach Horsuwan
changes: Initial baseline release of Stakeholder Needs and Requirements specification (RN-01 through RN-08)
RN-01 & RN-02: Defined fleet scalability, cost-effectiveness, and decentralized inter-robot communication needs
RN-03 & RN-04: Established locomotion/sensing consistency and modular hardware/software extensibility needs
RN-05 & RN-06: Specified fleet-level power/charging operations, obstacle avoidance, and cooperative transport needs
RN-07 & RN-08: Defined centralized experimental monitoring/telemetry and cross-disciplinary reproducibility needs

documents.title: Platform Requirements Description (PRD): Requirements for a Mobile Robot Platform in MARS Research
documents.author: Dhamdhawach Horsuwan
documents.summary: Defines platform capability requirements and operational use-case scenarios across 7 key subsystem areas: (1) Modularity and Extensibility, (2) Power Management, (3) Mobility and Manipulation, (4) Perception and Sensing, (5) Localization and State Estimation, (6) Multi-Agent Coordination and Communication, and (7) User Interface and Fleet Management.

versions.author: Dhamdhawach Horsuwan
changes: Initial baseline release of Platform Requirements & Use-Case Scenarios specification (5-page PDF)
Established operational context and commercial-grade usability/accessibility objectives for MARS fleets
Defined Section 1 (Modularity & Extensibility) and Section 2 (Power Regulation, BMS Protection, Exchangeable Battery Module, Fleet Charging, Power On/Off Control)
Defined Section 3 (Holonomic/Closed-Loop Locomotion & Collaborative Manipulation), Section 4 (Environmental Perception & Reciprocal Collision Avoidance), and Section 5 (Pose Estimation)
Defined Section 6 (Peer-to-Peer Inter-Robot Communication & Decentralized Network Topology) and Section 7 (Fleet Monitoring, Onboard Display/Button UI, Status LEDs, Telemetry Logging)
